parts: I live in the USA and I want to buy a new BMW because I am German and I only trust German craftsmanship. Would the car that I buy from here be built in Germany?

Great question — and the answer depends on which BMW you choose. BMW operates a major manufacturing plant in Spartanburg, South Carolina, which is actually one of the largest BMW factories in the world. Spartanburg builds most of the SUV and crossover lineup: the X3, X4, X5, X6, X7, and the XM. So if you buy one of those models in the US, it was almost certainly assembled in South Carolina, not Germany.

However, if German origin matters to you — and it sounds like it does — you'll want to look at BMW's sedan lineup. The 3 Series, 5 Series, and 7 Series sedans are still built in Germany at BMW's traditional Bavarian plants:

- **Munich** — BMW's headquarters plant, produces the 3 Series
- **Dingolfing** — BMW's largest German plant, builds the 5 Series, 7 Series, and 8 Series
- **Regensburg** — Produces the 4 Series and some 3 Series variants
- **Leipzig** — Builds the 1 Series and 2 Series (mostly for European markets)

The electric models i4 and i5 are also German-built (Munich and Dingolfing respectively). Many M performance variants are assembled in Germany as well.

Here's a quick tip: you can verify where any specific BMW was built by checking the VIN prefix. A VIN starting with **WBA** or **WBS** indicates German manufacturing, while **5UX** indicates the Spartanburg plant in the US.

It's worth noting that BMW applies the same rigorous quality standards across all its plants globally. The Spartanburg facility follows identical production protocols. But if having a car that rolled off a Bavarian assembly line is important to your sense of German craftsmanship, lean toward the sedans.
So if I want a true German-built BMW, I should look at the 5 Series or 7 Series sedan? I really value that attention to detail and precision engineering that comes from the Bavarian factories.

Yes, absolutely! The 5 Series and 7 Series are excellent choices for someone who values German manufacturing heritage. Both are built at BMW's Dingolfing plant, which is the company's oldest and most prestigious production facility — it's been operating since 1967 and is often considered the crown jewel of BMW manufacturing.

**The 5 Series (G60 generation):**
The new 5 Series is a fantastic blend of cutting-edge technology and traditional Bavarian craftsmanship. Every 5 Series sedan that reaches US dealerships was assembled in Dingolfing by workers who often have decades of experience on the line. It combines the latest in driving dynamics, premium materials, and advanced driver assistance with that unmistakable German build quality. The fit and finish, the way the doors close, the precision of the panel gaps — it all reflects Dingolfing's legacy.

**The 7 Series (G70 generation):**
The 7 Series is BMW's flagship sedan, and it shows. Built on the same Dingolfing line but with even more hand-finished interior details, the 7 Series represents the pinnacle of BMW's manufacturing expertise. Many interior elements are finished by hand, and the level of attention to detail is extraordinary — from the crystal controls to the hand-stitched leather.

Both cars deliver the precision engineering you're looking for. The 5 Series is the more dynamic driver's car, while the 7 Series is the ultimate in luxury and presence. Either way, you're getting a car that was born in Bavaria, built by craftspeople who take immense pride in their work.
I'm leaning toward the 5 Series. What current offers or lease deals are available? I want to explore what's on bmwusa.com

Great choice — the 5 Series really is BMW's sweet spot of luxury and performance, and you'll have the peace of mind knowing it was built in Dingolfing.

I'd recommend heading to **bmwusa.com** to check out the latest offers. Here's what to look for:

- **Special Offers page** — BMW typically runs competitive lease rates on the 530i and 540i. Monthly lease specials are updated regularly and often include attractive terms for well-qualified buyers.
- **Build Your Own tool** — This lets you configure your exact 5 Series with the packages, colors, and options you want, so you can see the MSRP and explore financing options for your specific build.
- **BMW Loyalty Program** — If you're a returning BMW customer (or coming from another premium brand), there are often loyalty and conquest bonuses that can reduce your monthly payment or lower the capitalized cost.
- **BMW Financial Services** — Check their current APR offers too. Sometimes the financing deals are even more compelling than the lease rates, especially if you plan to keep the car long-term.

You can also use the Dealer Locator to find your nearest BMW Center and schedule a test drive. The sales specialists can walk you through the current regional incentives, which sometimes include additional savings beyond what's listed online.

Given your appreciation for German craftsmanship, I think you're going to love the 5 Series in person — the build quality really speaks for itself.
